cards.title: Build the Shipward desk core (server + board)
cards.note: SCOPE NARROWED at the quick-dev step-01 checkpoint to the desk core: CAP-1,2,3,6,7,8,9 — serve.mjs, board with drag & drop, card dialog, activity strip, 3s live poll. Archive (SW-003), Raw data (SW-004) and the MCP server (SW-005) split out as separate cards. Built via bmad-quick-dev against _bmad-output/specs/spec-shipward/SPEC.md. Recreate the hi-fi prototype at design_handoff_shipward/design-reference/Shipward-Modernist.dc.html as a static no-build web app in shipward/public, served by shipward/serve.mjs (~60 lines, zero deps, port 4747): GET /api/tracker reads .shipward/tracker.json, PUT /api/tracker does an atomic write (tmp + rename). UI polls GET ~3s so Claude Code's direct file edits appear live. Four views: Board (4 columns + drag & drop), Archive, Raw data, Card dialog. Tokens in design_handoff_shipward/design-reference/assets/modernist-scoped.css — strip the #sw-1a scoping prefix. Radius 0 everywhere. .shipward/schema.json is normative. Full spec: design_handoff_shipward/README.md.

cards.title: Distill the design handoff into a SPEC contract
cards.note: Ran bmad-spec on design_handoff_shipward/. Output: _bmad-output/specs/spec-shipward/ — SPEC.md (10 capabilities), companions data-contract.md + interaction-rules.md, adopted companions README.md + CLAUDE.md, sources tracker.seed.json + seed.js. Both self-validate passes PASS. Decision: README adopted rather than transcribed, so the token table and screen specs stay single-sourced. Four open questions left for Alberto — MCP tag has no MCP behind it, card-delete contradicts CLAUDE.md 'never delete', shipped-this-month field precedence, projects[] editability. Skill was invoked by loading SKILL.md directly: the session skill registry is rooted at /Users/alberto/projects, so project-local .claude/skills are not callable via the Skill tool.

cards.title: MCP server so Claude Code reaches the tracker over MCP (stage B)
cards.note: SCOPE NARROWED to stage B at the step-02 token check (~2757 tokens vs a 1600 ceiling). Stage A shipped as SW-006. Remaining: shipward/mcp.mjs — zero-dep stdio JSON-RPC 2.0, protocol 2025-11-25, five verb tools (standup, log, start, done, sync) importing the rules from public/lib.js so the UI and Claude cannot drift; .mcp.json registration; mcp.test.mjs over a real pipe. Writes go through tracker-store.mjs, which is now cross-process safe. NO @modelcontextprotocol/sdk — zero-dep is an Always constraint; hand-roll the protocol.

cards.title: Cross-process safe tracker writes — shared store + lock
cards.note: Stage A of SW-005. Extracted read/validate/atomic-write into shipward/tracker-store.mjs behind an O_EXCL advisory lock spanning the whole read-modify-write; serve.mjs is now a client and its in-process promise chain is gone. That chain only protected same-process writes — the MCP server and Claude Code direct edits both sit outside it. Lock records pid+timestamp, aged out after 5s so a crashed holder cannot deadlock the desk. 34 tests pass: store.test.mjs spawns real child processes (12 concurrent writers all land, stale locks broken, fresh locks waited for not stolen, invalid mutations write nothing and still release); desk-core suite passes unchanged as the regression gate. ⚠️ PULLED BACK FROM REVIEW 2026-07-25: adversarial review REPRODUCED five failures — the lock does not hold. (1) Contended stale-break: 4 processes vs one stale lock, 9/25 trials LOST WRITES, because detect-and-break is three non-atomic steps and each breaker unlinks the previous winner’s fresh lock. (2) A 6s mutation gets its lock stolen at 5s; both processes exit 0 and one write vanishes silently. (3) A dangling symlink at the lock path spins acquire() forever at 100% CPU — two of three loop paths skip the deadline check. (4) replace() (every card drag) never re-reads under the lock, so a desk PUT erased a Claude write that had committed correctly. (5) rename resets file mode 600→644. Also: feed at exactly 200 makes validate() reject every subsequent write and freezes the tracker; lost in-process FIFO ordering; GET re-serializes instead of returning raw bytes. 34 tests passed throughout — none of them covered contention. || REWORKED after review: the lock was redesigned, not patched. Publish via write-scratch-then-link(): link is atomic AND never leaves an empty lock visible, which open(wx) did — under contention a process starved between create and stamp, waiters read a bodyless lock and broke a LIVE holder’s. Break a dead lock by rename (one atomic step) so two breakers cannot both win and delete each other’s fresh lock. Ownership token: a holder only ever releases the lock it took. Liveness (process.kill(pid,0)) over age, plus a utimes heartbeat — utimes not writeFile, because rewriting the body truncates it and reopens the same window. Every retry path now checks the deadline and sleeps (two used to spin at 100% CPU). Also: feed cap truncates instead of rejecting (rejection froze the tracker permanently at 200 entries); file mode preserved across rename; fsync before rename; read() distinguishes ENOENT from EACCES; GET returns raw bytes not a re-serialization; in-process FIFO queue restored in front of the lock; err.name instead of instanceof; orphan tmp and lock-scratch files swept on break. 41 tests pass. Stress: 25 trials x 4 contended writers against a stale lock = 0 lost writes, 0 leftovers (was 9/25 losing writes). 12-writer repro 12/12 across three runs.

cards.title: Prefer MCP in CLAUDE.md and make the header tag live
cards.note: Stage C of SW-005, depends on SW-005 stage B. Rewrite CLAUDE.md so the protocol prefers the MCP tools with direct file edits as the documented fallback (Alberto authorised this Ask First change at the SW-005 step-01 checkpoint). Drive the header MCP CONNECTED tag from an mcp.lastSeen heartbeat, stale after 150s, with a muted non-blinking disconnected variant. schema.json sets no additionalProperties, so the mcp key needs no schema change — verified. KNOWN TRADEOFF: a 60s heartbeat makes the committed tracker.json dirty in git about once a minute; the alternative is a .shipward/mcp-status.json sidecar.

cards.title: PUT /api/tracker is last-write-wins — decide if it should be
cards.note: REPRODUCED by adversarial review against a live server: desk GETs at T0, Claude Code appends a card via mutate() at T1 (correctly locked, committed), desk PUTs its T0 snapshot at T2 — PUT 200 and Claude’s card is GONE. The lock worked perfectly and the data was still destroyed, because replace() never re-reads under the lock: its base document came from an unlocked GET seconds earlier. This is the primary remaining loss path. It is also a CONTRADICTION between two live contracts. spec-mcp-tracker-server.md Always says two processes must never start a mutation from the same base document; spec-shipward-desk-core.md accepts no optimistic concurrency on PUT, last write wins, as a documented assumption. NEEDS ALBERTO: either add optimistic concurrency (If-Match on a version or etag, 409 on conflict, UI re-reads and retries) which is an Ask First change to the HTTP surface, or narrow the stage-A Always to say the lock protects mutate() callers only and PUT stays last-write-wins by design. Referenced from a comment in tracker-store.mjs replace(). || DECIDED by Alberto: add optimistic concurrency. GET returns an ETag (content hash); PUT requires If-Match and answers 409 with the current document when it does not match; the UI re-applies its mutation to the fresh document and retries once. This is the authorised Ask First change to the HTTP surface. [committed by Claude at T1] || SHIPPED: GET returns an ETag (sha256 of the file bytes, 16 hex chars, quoted). PUT requires If-Match — 428 without it — and the store compares it INSIDE the lock against what is on disk. Mismatch answers 409 carrying the document that actually won plus its ETag, so the client can re-apply rather than guess. The UI recovers automatically: commit() takes a mutation, not a snapshot, so on 409 it re-applies the same intent to the winning document and retries once; a second conflict adopts the winner and says so. VERIFIED end to end against the live server by replaying the exact scenario the review used to destroy data: desk GETs at T0, Claude commits via mutate() at T1, desk PUTs its T0 snapshot at T2 — now HTTP 409 and Claude’s write SURVIVES. In the browser: drag sends a well-formed If-Match; a forced stale etag produced 409 then 200 with the external write intact and no error shown. 45 tests pass. The old "concurrent writes never corrupt the file" test was rewritten — it asserted six concurrent PUTs from one base all succeed, which was the bug; it now asserts exactly one wins and the rest get 409.

cards.title: serve.test.mjs binds a fixed port and cannot run concurrently
cards.note: The sandbox server in serve.test.mjs hard-codes port 4749. A leftover server from an earlier or parallel run holds the port, the new server fails to bind, and the tests silently assert against the STALE server — observed here as three phantom failures (GET returning 200 for a missing tracker). Fix: bind port 0, read the assigned port back from the server, pass it to the tests. The sandbox server should also log bind failures rather than dying silently.
